newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on harvest and yield reports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on harvest and yield reports.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on harvest pressure and reports of better-than-expected yields, traders said.
New crop July reached a six-month low of $3.28 per bushel, equal to the level touched on December 5. The July also was closing in on a three-year low for a nearby CBOT wheat futures contract.

"Yields are much better than expected and quality is much better than expected in the hard red and soft red areas. The hardest thing in the world to do is pick a bottom in a down-trending market," said Charlie Sernatinger, analyst for E.D. and F. Man International.

Traders said aggressive combining over the weekend and persistent talk about the good crop being harvested in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat region led the way down. KCBT hard red winter wheat wheat tumbled sharply and reports continue of excellent yields in the early stages of the soft red winter wheat crop.
A new contract low of $3.51 a bushel was set in the May 1998 contract.
Wheat futures closed unchanged to five cents per bushel lower, with July down five at $3.29-3/4 a bushel.
Cash grain dealers Sunday said the hot and dry weather allowed aggressive harvesting of the Kansas hard red winter wheat crop and yield indications so far were above average.
The market dropped despite news USDA said U.S. wheat inspected for export during the week ended June 19 totaled 17.269 million bushels, above expectations for 9.0 million to 14.0 million.
Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders Report held no surprises, traders said.

As of Tuesday, non-commercials including funds, were short wheat by roughly 80.5 million bushels and long by roughly 37.9 million bushels. Commercials were short by 170.3 million and long by 195 million bushels.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 18,500 contracts, below the 23,587 traded Friday.
Cargill Inc sold 1.5 million bushels of July, Merrill Lynch Futures sold three million bushels of December and Prudential Securities sold 2.5 million bushels of December, traders said.
In spread dealings, Prudential Securities did two million bushels of July/September at 7-1/4 cents, premium September, traders said.

In wheat options, FIMAT Futures sold 400 September $3.50 calls at 7-1/2 to eight cents and sold 400 September $3.40 puts at 13-1/2 to 13-3/4 cents and Prudential Securities bought 400 September $4.40 calls at 5/8 cent, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,000 contracts, below the 6,565 traded Friday.
